lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Confirmed the forecast gain over the nested HAR-RV baseline with standard Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices.
- Joining 120 microstructure features point-in-time across six venues, deduplicating late prints and versioning each schema, built a feature store the team reused in two later projects.
- Annualized the signal's daily Sharpe ratio by multiplying it by 252 before reporting it to the desk.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.

- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation while maintaining the lab's shared cluster, organizing the weekly reading group and grading for two courses, which was downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Cut forecast error from 0.20 to 0.15, a 33% improvement, by adding realized-volatility features and an asymmetric loss.
- Improved the model's directional hit rate by 6% on 30 equity indices, from 52% to 58%, with a temporal convolutional model.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Use real contact details rather than placeholders in the final version.
Make the code link open directly to a polished GitHub profile or portfolio.
items.because: Readers should not have to navigate to it.

items.says: Add LinkedIn only if the profile is complete and consistent with the résumé.
Remove the code portfolio if it is weak or inactive.
items.because: An underdeveloped profile can hurt more than help.

items.says: Use “candidate” only if you have formally advanced to candidacy.
items.because: Otherwise, use the degree program designation.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant research area, dissertation topic, or advisor.
items.because: It could help for quant roles.

items.says: Verify that the expected graduation date is accurate and consistent across applications.
Add honors or GPA only if they are strong and useful.
Shorten the B.S. line if space becomes tight.
items.because: The Ph.D. carries more weight.

items.says: Move the bakery role into Additional Experience or reduce it to one bullet.
items.because: Its position above the quant internship may obscure the professional narrative.

items.says: Check that the bakery role’s chronology is accurate.
items.because: Recruiters may wonder how the role fits with the Ph.D. and quant career path.

items.says: Change “labour” to “labor.”
items.because: It would be consistent with a U.S.-based résumé.

items.says: Strengthen the budget result with the size or difficulty of the achievement.
items.because: “Within budget” only indicates meeting a requirement.

items.says: Give routine shift responsibilities less space than high-value quantitative work.
Define the period for the 12% and 7% production figures.
items.because: The percentages need clearer context.

items.says: Distinguish a five-percentage-point reduction from an approximately 42% relative reduction.
items.because: The two should not be blurred.

items.says: Clarify whether the Sharpe improvement belongs to the signal, a combined backtest, or the actual desk book.
items.because: “Desk book’s Sharpe ratio” can imply a live result despite the stated backtest.

items.says: Confirm that “out-of-sample” is technically accurate.
items.because: The 18-month period may have been repeatedly used for model selection.

items.says: Ensure the Sharpe figures use the correct annualization methodology.
items.because: The annualization bullet elsewhere contains a mistake.

items.says: Define turnover using the desk’s convention.
items.because: Turnover definitions vary.

items.says: Clarify whether the slippage reduction came from realized trading or a transaction-cost model.
Give “keeping 90% of gross returns” a precise comparison point.
items.because: The unsmoothed strategy might be the intended comparison.

items.says: Remove “standard” unless the exact testing procedure can be defended.
Recheck whether the Diebold–Mariano test is valid for the nested-model comparison.
items.because: Standard DM inference can be problematic in nested settings.

items.says: Identify the forecast metric being tested.
items.because: “Forecast gain” is too vague for a technical audience.

items.says: Account for serial dependence, cross-index dependence, and multiple comparisons.
items.because: The bullet claims significance across 30 indices.

items.says: Check that “30 indices” is consistent with the earlier reference to liquid index futures.
Fix the sentence structure and lead with the feature store.
items.because: The long introductory phrase delays the main action and obscures ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether you built the store independently or contributed to a team system.
Make sure “six venues” is plausible for the instruments described elsewhere.
Multiplying daily Sharpe by 252 is mathematically wrong.
items.because: Conventional scaling uses the square root of 252, subject to assumptions about return dependence.

items.says: Routine Sharpe-ratio reporting is not a résumé-worthy accomplishment.
items.because: It describes reporting rather than impact.

items.says: Clarify the onboarding impact if it can be supported.
items.because: The wording may imply that the documentation alone caused onboarding to take one week.

items.says: Prioritize this below modeling, validation, and infrastructure bullets.
Specify the main source of the simulation speedup, if available.
items.because: Technical reviewers will care how it was achieved.

items.says: Ensure the three-day and five-hour measurements used comparable hardware and workload.
Remove first-person phrasing.
items.because: It is inconsistent with the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Consider moving the achievement into a Publications or Research section.
items.because: A title, preprint, or coauthors could be presented there.

items.says: Emphasize the mathematical contribution rather than “Section 3.”
items.because: The section number is less useful.

items.says: Verify that “under review at JASA” is current.
items.because: The paper’s status may change.

items.says: Avoid implying sole ownership if the result was collaborative.
Add context for the 4.8/5 rating if available.
items.because: Without a response count or comparison, it may appear selectively reported.

items.says: Consider a separate teaching entry if this was formally a teaching assistant role.
items.because: It may not belong under the research assistantship.

items.says: Give this bullet lower priority if space is tight on an industry résumé.
items.because: Research and engineering achievements are more important there.

items.says: Split the package achievement from the unrelated service responsibilities.
items.because: The line combines four responsibilities and dilutes the software achievement.

items.says: Keep the package and download metric together.
items.because: The current wording leaves what was downloaded unclear.

items.says: Remove or heavily reduce cluster maintenance if it duplicates the simulation-pipeline bullet.
Remove reading-group organization and grading unless they matter to the target role.
Verify the source and definition of the 3,000 downloads.
items.because: Counts can include automated mirrors or CI systems.

items.says: Add a repository, paper, or technical-report link if the work is public and polished.
Indicate the project’s current output or status.
items.because: It has been ongoing since January 2024.

items.says: Make clear whether the independent volatility project is separate from the Northpeak internship.
items.because: The shared baseline, 30 indices, and similar language could suggest duplicated or confidential work.

items.says: Do not expose employer data, methods, or results through the independent project.
items.because: Parts of the project may overlap with the internship.

items.says: Clarify the evaluation period, forecast horizon, and aggregation method if space permits.
Report statistical significance only if the test is valid and appropriately adjusted.
Ensure the HAR-RV baseline was tuned and evaluated fairly.
items.because: Technical interviewers may examine this common benchmark closely.

items.says: Confirm that “30 equity indices” is the correct asset description.
The reduction from 0.20 to 0.15 is 25%, not 33%.
Name the forecast-error metric.
items.because: Raw numbers have little meaning without a scale and definition.

items.says: Clarify whether this is a separate experiment from the 7% QLIKE result.
Remove the bullet if it merely restates the first result.
items.because: It would add no distinct insight.

items.says: Separate the effects of the features and asymmetric loss if an ablation cannot attribute the gain to both.
The move from 52% to 58% is six percentage points, not 6%.
items.because: Its relative increase is approximately 11.5%.

items.says: Define “directional” for volatility forecasting.
Avoid repeating the model type and 30-index scope.
items.because: Those facts are established directly above.

items.says: State whether 58% is statistically distinguishable from 50%.
items.because: Otherwise the number may not be persuasive.

items.says: Keep directional accuracy only if it matters to the strategy or research objective.
Use the competition’s exact official name if it can be disclosed.
Add a Kaggle profile or competition link.
items.because: It would verify the result.

items.says: Consider omitting “top 2%.”
items.because: The exact placement already communicates the result.

items.says: Verify that 2,900 is the final number of eligible teams.
items.because: It might instead count total registrations.

items.says: Make explicit that 41st was the private or final leaderboard placement.
items.because: The bullet does so only partly.

items.says: Be precise about the validation-leakage claim.
items.because: Closing the local-to-leaderboard gap shows better alignment but does not by itself prove leakage was eliminated.

items.says: Explain the grouping unit if it is technically important and can be stated briefly.
Identify the score scale.
items.because: Otherwise a 0.02 gap is hard to interpret.

items.says: Ensure permutation importance did not use the final holdout or private leaderboard feedback.
Ensure “without losing validation score” reflects an untouched validation set.
items.because: Repeated tuning on the same folds would weaken the claim.

items.says: Give this bullet lower priority if space is tight.
items.because: It is less distinctive than the placement and validation bullets.

items.says: Organize the skills by type.
items.because: Python and R are languages, PyTorch is a framework, and Kafka is data infrastructure.

items.says: Retain Kafka only if you have hands-on use you can discuss.
items.because: Nothing in the experience section currently supports it.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “econometrics.”

items.says: Keep the hyphenation of “time-series” consistent.
Ensure each listed method is supported by an experience or project bullet.
Consider adding relevant demonstrated methods.
items.because: Volatility forecasting, market microstructure, Monte Carlo simulation, or statistical testing may better reflect the work.

items.says: Move “gradient boosting” under modeling techniques.
items.because: It may fit better there than under broad statistical methods.

items.says: Create separate Relevant Experience and Additional Experience sections.
items.because: The quant internship and research work should receive priority without hiding the bakery role.

items.says: Consider a Publications section.
items.because: It could hold the JASA submission and other public research output.

items.says: Put the strongest quant evidence nearer the top.
items.because: Northpeak, statistical research, volatility forecasting, and Kaggle deserve priority.

items.says: Standardize date punctuation and use en dashes consistently.
